newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Arafat begin summit on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat begin summit on Hebron.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat began a meeting on Wednesday to resolve disputes still blocking a Hebron deal.

The two men arrived at the Erez crossing between Israel and the Gaza strip for talks on finally extending Palestinian rule to Hebron 10 months after the due date for Israel's troop withdrawal from most of the West Bank town.
Hours earlier, Israeli and Palestinian negotiators ended U.S.-mediated talks saying the leaders would have to clear final hurdles before wrapping up the agreement.
"We hope there will be a signing tonight. There are still some minor issues which need to be resolved," PLO negotiator Mahmoud Abbas told reporters in Jerusalem.

The U.S. consul-general in Jerusalem, Edward Abington, was also upbeat that an accord on Israel's withdrawal was in sight. "I think there's a very good chance we'll see an agreement tonight. Everything is in good shape," he said.

Violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June have delayed the Jewish state's pullback from Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint where some 400 militant Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Arabs.
